 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Bibek Chaudhuri
 Oral Order
Heard learned Advocate for the petitioner as well as learned APP for the State.

2. The petitioner has approached this Court for issuance of a writ in the nature of certiorari,
directing the respondent authorities to quash F.I.R. in connection with Gardanibagh P.S. Case No.
346 of 2018, dated 21.08.2018, instituted against the petitioner under Section 7 of the Essential Commodities Act.
3. The allegation made out in the FIR, in brief, is that the FIR is registered under Section 7 of the Essential Commodities Act (E.C. Act) include the seizure of rice by the Patna High Court CR.
WJC No.104 of 2021(4) dt.15-03-2024 Supply Inspector due to the allegation that the seized rice, believed to be similar to subsidized rice, was found in the possession of the petitioner.

This led to the filing of the FIR by the Supply Inspector, alleging a violation of the provisions of the E.C. Act regarding the possession of essential commodities.
4. It is asserted by the Petitioner that the legality, validity, and justification of the actions taken by the respondent authorities, particularly respondent no. 7, contended by the petitioner that they are not a Public Distribution System (PDS) dealer but a trader of foodgrains, conducting business under the name and style of M/S Shivam Traders.

It is also contended by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that rice and wheat do not fall under any control order, and therefore, Section 7 of the Anil Kumar @ Anil Saw vs The State Of Bihar on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58732537/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Essential Commodities Act is not applicable to them.
Therefore, the petitioner was entitled to purchase and sell rice from the open market.

5. It is pointed out by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that he has annexed series of cash memos and invoices in Annexure-2 series, showing that he purchased the seized foodgrains from various traders.
Therefore, the petitioner has not violated any provision of Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act.
Accordingly, he cannot be held liable under Patna High Court CR.
WJC No.104 of 2021(4) dt.15-03-2024 Section 7 of the said Act.
It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that he has not cheated any person.
There is no complaint against the petitioner alleging cheating in the course of business.
Merely, storing rice, which partly resembles with the subsidised rice, the petitioner cannot be held liable under Section 7 of the Essential Commodities Act.

6. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate for the petitioner refers to the following unreported decisions of this Court, passed by the Coordinate Benches:-
I. Dilip Kumar Vrs.
The State of Bihar (Criminal Miscellaneous No. 15437 of 2014),

decided on 11th April, 2018.
II. Sandip Kumar Jaiswal @ Sandip Jaiswal Vrs.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
III. Arjun Prasad @ Arbind Kumar (Criminal Miscellaneous No. 12491 of 2022),
decided on 8th February, 2024.
7. Learned Advocate for the State has not raised any legal point against the Judgments passed by this Court in the above mentioned cases.
8. After perusal of the documents and careful consideration of the submissions made by the petitioner and the Patna High Court CR.
WJC No.104 of 2021(4) dt.15-03-2024 relevant legal provisions and precedents cited
, this Hon'ble Court finds merit in the petitioner's contentions.
The actions of the respondent authorities appear to lack legal justification and may indeed constitute an abuse of power.

9. This Court concurs with the view of the Coordinate Benches on the issue that for storing rice in the godown and shop by the petitioner, he cannot be held liable under Section 7 of the Essential Commodities Act and Section 420 of the I.P.C.
10.
For the reasons stated above, I do not find any merit in the instant F.I.R. and accordingly, the F.I.R. is quashed.
11. The instant writ petition is accordingly disposed of.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J) uttam/-
